paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמִתְאֹ֣נְנִ֔ים רַ֖ע בְּאָזְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ וַיִּ֣חַר אַפּ֔וֹ וַתִּבְעַר־בָּם֙ אֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אכַל בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And the people were like those who complain, evil in the ears of YHWH; and YHWH heard, and his anger was kindled, and the fire of YHWH burned among them and consumed at the edge of the camp.

notes.official: *wayhî hāʿām kəmiṯʾōnənîm raʿ bəʾoznê YHWH* 'And the people were like those who complain, evil in the ears of YHWH': *miṯʾōnənîm* is a rare Hithpolel ('complain, murmur'; elsewhere only Lam 3:39). *wattiḇʿar-bām ʾēš YHWH* 'and the fire of YHWH burned among them' (central `esh-yhwh-fire-of-yhwh`, as 1 Kgs 18:38). *biqṣēh hammaḥăneh* 'at the edge of the camp'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֖ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּשְׁקַ֖ע הָאֵֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: And the people cried out to Moses; and Moses prayed to YHWH, and the fire died down.

notes.official: *wayyiṯpallēl mōšeh* 'and Moses prayed' (central `hithpallel-first-prayer-occurrence`): Moses intercedes, as in 14:13-19 and 21:7. *wattišqaʿ hāʾēš* 'and the fire died down' (literally 'sank').

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא תַּבְעֵרָ֑ה כִּֽי־בָעֲרָ֥ה בָ֖ם אֵ֥שׁ יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the name of that place was called Tav'erah (Burning), because the fire of YHWH burned among them.

notes.official: *wayyiqrāʾ šēm-hammāqôm hahûʾ taḇʿērâ kî-ḇāʿărâ bām ʾēš YHWH* 'And the name of that place was called Tav'erah (Burning), because the fire of YHWH burned among them'. 'Tav'erah' = Taberah (ASV). Because the verse states the etymology in a causal clause, the name is glossed under the Torah rule (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-numbers-11`), as 'Qivrot-haTa'avah (Graves of Craving)' at v 34. The impersonal 'was called' follows the ASV and central `al-ken-qara-shemah-aetiological-naming-formula-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: וְהָֽאסַפְסֻף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ הִתְאַוּ֖וּ תַּאֲוָ֑ה וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ וַיִּבְכּ֗וּ גַּ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י יַאֲכִלֵ֖נוּ בָּשָֽׂר׃

i18n.en: And the rabble that was among them craved a craving; and the children of Yisra'el also wept again and said, "Who will give us meat to eat?

notes.official: *wəhāʾsap̄sup̄* 'the rabble' (ASV 'the mixed multitude'): a reduplicated noun, 'riff-raff', found only here, often connected with the *ʿēreḇ raḇ* 'mixed multitude' of Ex 12:38. *hiṯʾawwû taʾăwâ* 'craved a craving': a cognate accusative of the root *ʾwh*, which also gives the name Qivrot-haTa'avah in v 34. *mî yaʾăḵilēnû bāśār* 'Who will give us meat to eat?'

paragraphs.text: זָכַ֙רְנוּ֙ אֶת־הַדָּגָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נֹאכַ֥ל בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם חִנָּ֑ם אֵ֣ת הַקִּשֻּׁאִ֗ים וְאֵת֙ הָֽאֲבַטִּחִ֔ים וְאֶת־הֶחָצִ֥יר וְאֶת־הַבְּצָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַשּׁוּמִֽים׃

i18n.en: We remember the fish which we ate in Mitsrayim for nothing, the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic;

notes.official: *ḥinnām* 'for nothing' (central `chinnam`): in memory, the food of Egypt cost nothing. 'Mitsrayim' = Egypt (central `mitsrayim`). The list (cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, garlic) names Egyptian garden produce.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֛ה נַפְשֵׁ֥נוּ יְבֵשָׁ֖ה אֵ֣ין כֹּ֑ל בִּלְתִּ֖י אֶל־הַמָּ֥ן עֵינֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: but now our appetite is dried up; there is nothing at all, except this manna before our eyes."

notes.official: *wəʿattâ nap̄šēnû yəḇēšâ* 'but now our appetite is dried up': *nep̄eš* here is the throat and the appetite it stands for (HALOT *nep̄eš* 1-2; NJPS 'our gullets are shriveled'; NRSV 'our strength is dried up'). The ASV 'our soul is dried away' is replaced under `nefesh-scope-torah`. *ʾên kōl biltî ʾel-hammān ʿênênû* 'there is nothing at all, except this manna before our eyes' (central `mannah-bread-from-heaven-ex-16-quranic-and-nt-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`).

paragraphs.text: וְהַמָּ֕ן כִּזְרַע־גַּ֖ד ה֑וּא וְעֵינ֖וֹ כְּעֵ֥ין הַבְּדֹֽלַח׃

i18n.en: Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium.

notes.official:
*wəhammān kizraʿ-gaḏ hûʾ wəʿênô kəʿên habbəḏōlaḥ* 'Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium': *ʿayin* 'eye' is used for 'look, appearance' (ASV 'the appearance thereof'). *bəḏōlaḥ* is the aromatic resin bdellium, or possibly a pale gem (Gen 2:12). Vv 7-9 interrupt the complaint with a description of the manna that answers it: the food the people despise is fine and plentiful (central `mannah-bread-from-heaven-ex-16-quranic-and-nt-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`; cf. Ex 16:14, 31).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) cites Num 11:7-8 as 'the very exact description of the manna that your chemists could reconstitute', quoting 'And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium (…) and the taste of it was as the taste of a delicacy made with oil', and reads the manna as a chemical food that the creators preferred to fresh produce. The line describes the substance as the Hebrew does and does not encode that reading. The central manna entry's disavowal (iii) applies.

paragraphs.text: שָׁטוּ֩ הָעָ֨ם וְלָֽקְט֜וּ וְטָחֲנ֣וּ בָרֵחַ֗יִם א֤וֹ דָכוּ֙ בַּמְּדֹכָ֔ה וּבִשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּפָּר֔וּר וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ עֻג֑וֹת וְהָיָ֣ה טַעְמ֔וֹ כְּטַ֖עַם לְשַׁ֥ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן׃

i18n.en: The people went about and gathered it, and ground it in mills or pounded it in a mortar, and boiled it in pots and made cakes of it; and its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.

notes.official: *šāṭû hāʿām wəlāqəṭû* 'The people went about and gathered it'; the verse lists grinding in mills (*bārēḥayim*), pounding in a mortar (*bammədōḵâ*), boiling in pots and baking cakes (*ʿugôṯ*). *wəhāyâ ṭaʿmô kəṭaʿam ləšaḏ haššāmen* 'and its taste was like the taste of fresh oil': *ləšaḏ* is uncertain (elsewhere only Ps 32:4, 'my vigour' or 'my moisture'). The ASV 'fresh oil' takes it as the moisture or richness of oil. The LXX has *enkris ex elaiou* 'a cake made with oil', NJPS 'rich cream' and NRSV 'cakes baked with oil'. The ASV is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-numbers-11`). Ex 16:31 describes the taste as 'wafers made with honey'. The canon's English 'a delicacy made with oil' (French « une friandise à l'huile ») follows the LXX tradition; see the reception note at v 7.

paragraphs.text: וּבְרֶ֧דֶת הַטַּ֛ל עַל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה יֵרֵ֥ד הַמָּ֖ן עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell upon it.

notes.official: *ûḇəreḏeṯ haṭṭal ... yērēḏ hammān ʿālāyw* 'And when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell upon it', as Ex 16:13-14 describes the layer of dew.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־הָעָ֗ם בֹּכֶה֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔יו אִ֖ישׁ לְפֶ֣תַח אָהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ מְאֹ֔ד וּבְעֵינֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה רָֽע׃

i18n.en: And Moses heard the people weeping by their families, each man at the entrance of his tent; and the anger of YHWH was kindled greatly, and in the eyes of Moses it was evil.

notes.official: *bōḵeh ləmišpəḥōṯāyw* 'weeping by their families'. *ûḇəʿênê mōšeh rāʿ* 'and in the eyes of Moses it was evil': the subject may be the people's weeping or YHWH's anger. NJPS reads 'Moses was distressed'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה לָמָ֤ה הֲרֵעֹ֙תָ֙ לְעַבְדֶּ֔ךָ וְלָ֛מָּה לֹא־מָצָ֥תִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ לָשׂ֗וּם אֶת־מַשָּׂ֛א כָּל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה עָלָֽי׃

i18n.en: And Moses said to YHWH, "Why have you dealt ill with your servant? And why have I not found favor in your sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?

notes.official: *lāmâ hărēʿōṯā ləʿaḇdeḵā* 'Why have you dealt ill with your servant?' *lōʾ-māṣāṯî ḥēn bəʿêneyḵā* 'have I not found favor in your sight' (central `matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula`). *maśśāʾ* 'the burden': the word links Moses' complaint (vv 11, 17) with the verb *nāśāʾ* 'carry' of v 12.

paragraphs.text: הֶאָנֹכִ֣י הָרִ֗יתִי אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אִם־אָנֹכִ֖י יְלִדְתִּ֑יהוּ כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֨ר אֵלַ֜י שָׂאֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקֶ֗ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשָּׂ֤א הָאֹמֵן֙ אֶת־הַיֹּנֵ֔ק עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתָּ לַאֲבֹתָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me, 'Carry them in your bosom, as a nursing father carries the sucking child,' to the land which you swore to their fathers?

notes.official: *heʾānōḵî hārîṯî ... ʾim-ʾānōḵî yəliḏtîhû* 'Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them?': Moses uses the verbs of a mother and implies that YHWH is the people's parent. *kaʾăšer yiśśāʾ hāʾōmēn ʾeṯ-hayyōnēq* 'as a nursing father carries the sucking child': *ʾōmēn* is masculine, a male guardian or foster-father (2 Kgs 10:1, 5; Isa 49:23), so the line keeps the ASV's 'nursing father' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-numbers-11`). The quoted command is in single marks.

paragraphs.text: מֵאַ֤יִן לִי֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר לָתֵ֖ת לְכָל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־יִבְכּ֤וּ עָלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנָה־לָּ֥נוּ בָשָׂ֖ר וְנֹאכֵֽלָה׃

i18n.en: Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? For they weep to me, saying, 'Give us meat, that we may eat.'

notes.official: *mēʾayin lî bāśār* 'Where am I to get meat?' The people's demand is quoted in single marks inside Moses' speech.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־אוּכַ֤ל אָנֹכִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֥י כָבֵ֖ד מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

i18n.en: I am not able to carry all this people alone, for it is too heavy for me.

notes.official: *lāśēʾṯ ... kî ḵāḇēḏ mimmennî* 'to carry ... for it is too heavy for me': the vocabulary of burden returns in YHWH's answer (v 17) and in Jethro's advice of Ex 18:18.

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־כָּ֣כָה ׀ אַתְּ־עֹ֣שֶׂה לִּ֗י הָרְגֵ֤נִי נָא֙ הָרֹ֔ג אִם־מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְאַל־אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּרָעָתִֽי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And if you deal thus with me, kill me, I pray, outright, if I have found favor in your sight, and let me not look on my wretchedness."

notes.official: *wəʾim-kāḵâ ʾatt-ʿōśeh llî* 'And if you deal thus with me': *ʾatt* is the short spelling of the second-person masculine pronoun (as Deut 5:24; Ezek 28:14), which some read as feminine. *hārəḡēnî nāʾ hārōḡ* 'kill me, I pray, outright'. *wəʾal-ʾerʾeh bərāʿāṯî* 'and let me not look on my wretchedness'. Rabbinic tradition lists this phrase among the *tiqqunê sôp̄ərîm* (Mekhilta on Ex 15:7; the Masorah): the original is said to have read *bərāʿāṯəḵā* 'your evil', which scribes changed out of reverence. The line translates the MT, as genesis-woh does at the tiqqun of Gen 18:22 (central `tiqun-soferim-yhwh-stood-before-abraham`; `mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-numbers-11`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶסְפָה־לִּ֞י שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִישׁ֮ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי־הֵ֛ם זִקְנֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם וְשֹׁטְרָ֑יו וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֥וּ שָׁ֖ם עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Yisra'el, whom you know to be the elders of the people and its officers; and bring them to the tent of meeting, and let them present themselves there with you.

notes.official: *ʾespāh-llî šiḇʿîm ʾîš mizziqnê yiśrāʾēl* 'Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Yisra'el': 'seventy', as exodus-woh prints at Ex 24:1, 9, the other passage with seventy elders. Central shivim-nefesh-seventy-souls-foundational-number-LXX-variant keeps the archaic 'threescore and ten' for the genealogical count of Gen 46:27 and does not govern here. *wəšōṭərāyw* 'and its officers'. *wəhiṯyaṣṣəḇû šām ʿimmāḵ* 'and let them present themselves there with you' (central `mit'yatzev-al-YHWH`, whose rationale names this verse; ASV 'that they may stand there with thee').

paragraphs.text: וְיָרַדְתִּ֗י וְדִבַּרְתִּ֣י עִמְּךָ֮ שָׁם֒ וְאָצַלְתִּ֗י מִן־הָר֛וּחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָשְׂא֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּמַשָּׂ֣א הָעָ֔ם וְלֹא־תִשָּׂ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And I will come down and speak with you there; and I will take some of the spirit that is upon you and put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, so that you do not bear it yourself alone.

notes.official: *wəyāraḏtî* 'And I will come down' (central `vayered-yhwh`). *wəʾāṣaltî min-hārûaḥ ʾăšer ʿāleyḵā wəśamtî ʿălêhem* 'and I will take some of the spirit that is upon you and put it upon them': *ʾāṣal* is 'to set aside, withdraw a portion'. Moses' *rûaḥ* is apportioned without being diminished, as the rabbinic image of a lamp lighting other lamps puts it (Sifre Num 93). The line prints lower-case 'spirit' (ASV 'the Spirit'), as genesis-woh does for the *rûaḥ* in a person (Gen 41:38), under overlay `ruach-spirit-on-the-elders-numbers-11`. 2 Kgs 2:9, 15 ('a double portion of your ruach'; 'the ruach of Eliyahu rests on Elisha') is the nearest parallel, which the Kings volumes transliterate. *wənāśəʾû ʾittəḵā bəmaśśāʾ hāʿām* 'and they shall bear the burden of the people with you', answering Moses' complaint in vv 11-14.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־הָעָ֨ם תֹּאמַ֜ר הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמָחָר֮ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֣ם בָּשָׂר֒ כִּ֡י בְּכִיתֶם֩ בְּאָזְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֤י יַאֲכִלֵ֙נוּ֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּי־ט֥וֹב לָ֖נוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְנָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וַאֲכַלְתֶּֽם׃

i18n.en: And to the people you shall say, 'Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat; for you have wept in the ears of YHWH, saying, "Who will give us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Mitsrayim." Therefore YHWH will give you meat, and you shall eat.

notes.official: *hiṯqaddəšû ləmāḥār* 'Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow', as before the Sinai theophany (Ex 19:10-15). The irony is that the meat will be a punishment (vv 19-20, 33). The people's words are quoted in double marks inside the single marks of YHWH's message (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: לֹ֣א י֥וֹם אֶחָ֛ד תֹּאכְל֖וּן וְלֹ֣א יוֹמָ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א ׀ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה יָמִ֗ים וְלֹא֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה יָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֖א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: You shall eat not one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,

notes.official: The count by ones, twos, fives, tens and twenties builds to the month of v 20.

paragraphs.text: עַ֣ד ׀ חֹ֣דֶשׁ יָמִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא֙ מֵֽאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְזָרָ֑א יַ֗עַן כִּֽי־מְאַסְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֔ם וַתִּבְכּ֤וּ לְפָנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה יָצָ֥אנוּ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: but a whole month, until it comes out at your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you have rejected YHWH who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, "Why did we come out of Mitsrayim?"'"

notes.official: *ʿaḏ ʾăšer-yēṣēʾ mēʾappəḵem wəhāyâ lāḵem ləzārāʾ* 'until it comes out at your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you': *zārāʾ* 'loathing' occurs only here. *yaʿan kî-məʾastem ʾeṯ-YHWH ʾăšer bəqirbəḵem* 'because you have rejected YHWH who is among you': the craving for Egypt's food is treated as a rejection of YHWH himself.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ מֹשֶׁה֒ שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֙לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֗רְתָּ בָּשָׂר֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם וְאָכְל֖וּ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Moses said, "The people among whom I am are six hundred thousand on foot; and you have said, 'I will give them meat, that they may eat a whole month.'

notes.official: *šēš-mēʾôṯ ʾelep̄ raḡlî* 'six hundred thousand on foot', the census figure of Ex 12:37 (cf. Num 1:46). Moses quotes YHWH's promise back to him in single marks.

paragraphs.text: הֲצֹ֧אן וּבָקָ֛ר יִשָּׁחֵ֥ט לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֣א לָהֶ֑ם אִ֣ם אֶֽת־כָּל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֛ם יֵאָסֵ֥ף לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֥א לָהֶֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, to suffice them? Or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to suffice them?"

notes.official: *hăṣōʾn ûḇāqār yiššāḥēṭ lāhem ûmāṣāʾ lāhem* 'Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, to suffice them?' The repeated *ûmāṣāʾ lāhem* is literally 'and it would be found for them', i.e. 'would it be enough'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הֲיַ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה תִּקְצָ֑ר עַתָּ֥ה תִרְאֶ֛ה הֲיִקְרְךָ֥ דְבָרִ֖י אִם־לֹֽא׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Is the hand of YHWH too short? Now you shall see whether my word comes to pass for you or not."

notes.official: *hăyaḏ YHWH tiqṣār* 'Is the hand of YHWH too short?' (central `yad-yhwh`): the image of power that cannot reach recurs at Isa 50:2 and 59:1. *hăyiqrəḵā dəḇārî* 'whether my word comes to pass for you'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֞ף שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֹתָ֖ם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הָאֹֽהֶל׃

i18n.en: And Moses went out and told the people the words of YHWH; and he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them around the tent.

notes.official: *wayyaʿămēḏ ʾōṯām səḇîḇōṯ hāʾōhel* 'and set them around the tent': in this narrative the tent of meeting stands outside the camp (v 26; cf. Ex 33:7-11), not at its centre as in Num 2.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֨רֶד יְהוָ֥ה ׀ בֶּעָנָן֮ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָיו֒ וַיָּ֗אצֶל מִן־הָר֙וּחַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַיִּתֵּ֕ן עַל־שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ הַזְּקֵנִ֑ים וַיְהִ֗י כְּנ֤וֹחַ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָר֔וּחַ וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יָסָֽפוּ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was upon him and put it upon the seventy elders; and it came to pass, when the spirit rested upon them, that they prophesied, but they did not do so again.

notes.official: *wayyēreḏ YHWH beʿānān* 'And YHWH came down in the cloud' (central `vayered-yhwh`; cf. Ex 33:9; Num 12:5). *wayyāʾṣel min-hārûaḥ* 'and took some of the spirit' (overlay `ruach-spirit-on-the-elders-numbers-11`). *kənôaḥ ʿălêhem hārûaḥ* 'when the spirit rested upon them' (*nûaḥ*, as 2 Kgs 2:15). *wayyiṯnabbəʾû wəlōʾ yāsāp̄û* 'they prophesied, but they did not do so again': the MT *yāsāp̄û* is from *yāsap̄* 'add, do again' (ASV 'but they did so no more'). Targum Onqelos and the Vulgate read it as from *sûp̄* 'cease' ('and they did not cease'). The line translates the MT (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`): the prophesying was a one-time sign of the endowment, not a lasting office.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשָּׁאֲר֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי־אֲנָשִׁ֣ים ׀ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֡ה שֵׁ֣ם הָאֶחָ֣ד ׀ אֶלְדָּ֡ד וְשֵׁם֩ הַשֵּׁנִ֨י מֵידָ֜ד וַתָּ֧נַח עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם הָר֗וּחַ וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ בַּכְּתֻבִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָצְא֖וּ הָאֹ֑הֱלָה וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: But two men remained in the camp; the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad; and the spirit rested upon them (they were among those who were registered, but they had not gone out to the tent), and they prophesied in the camp.

notes.official: 'Eldad' and 'Medad' are identical in both forms (ASV). *wəhēmmâ bakkəṯuḇîm* 'they were among those who were registered': they were on the list of the seventy but had stayed in the camp. *wattānaḥ ʿălêhem hārûaḥ* 'and the spirit rested upon them' (overlay `ruach-spirit-on-the-elders-numbers-11`): the endowment does not depend on presence at the tent.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣רָץ הַנַּ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לְמֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֶלְדָּ֣ד וּמֵידָ֔ד מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And a young man ran and told Moses, and said, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp."

notes.official: *hannaʿar* 'a young man': the article marks a particular attendant, whom the narrative does not name.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֜עַן יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֗וּן מְשָׁרֵ֥ת מֹשֶׁ֛ה מִבְּחֻרָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנִ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה כְּלָאֵֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua the son of Nun, the attendant of Moses from his youth, answered and said, "My lord Moses, restrain them."

notes.official: 'Yehoshua' = Joshua; 'Nun' identical (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`). *məšārēṯ mōšeh mibbəḥurāyw* 'the attendant of Moses from his youth': the vocalisation is that of the abstract plural *bəḥurîm* 'youth' (BDB), and NJPS reads 'Moses' attendant from his youth'. The ASV's 'one of his chosen men' takes the word as *baḥûrîm* 'young men', which the MT pointing does not support (overlay `lexical-cruxes-numbers-11`). Ex 33:11 likewise calls Yehoshua a *naʿar* and Moses' attendant. *ʾăḏōnî mōšeh kəlāʾēm* 'My lord Moses, restrain them' (ASV 'forbid them').

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַֽמְקַנֵּ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לִ֑י וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן כָּל־עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ נְבִיאִ֔ים כִּי־יִתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־רוּח֖וֹ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Moses said to him, "Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the people of YHWH were prophets, that YHWH would put his spirit upon them!"

notes.official: *haməqannēʾ ʾattâ lî* 'Are you jealous for my sake?' *ûmî yittēn kol-ʿam YHWH nəḇîʾîm kî-yittēn YHWH ʾeṯ-rûḥô ʿălêhem* 'Would that all the people of YHWH were prophets, that YHWH would put his spirit upon them!' (central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`; overlay `ruach-spirit-on-the-elders-numbers-11`). Joel 3:1-2 (ET 2:28-29) takes up the wish as a promise. 'his spirit' is lower case, as in vv 17, 25.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּאָסֵ֥ף מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה ה֖וּא וְזִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Moses withdrew into the camp, he and the elders of Yisra'el.

notes.official: *wayyēʾāsēp̄ mōšeh ʾel-hammaḥăneh* 'And Moses withdrew into the camp': the Niphal of *ʾāsap̄* 'be gathered', here 'return'.

paragraphs.text: וְר֜וּחַ נָסַ֣ע ׀ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֣גָז שַׂלְוִים֮ מִן־הַיָּם֒ וַיִּטֹּ֨שׁ עַל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה כְּדֶ֧רֶךְ י֣וֹם כֹּ֗ה וּכְדֶ֤רֶךְ יוֹם֙ כֹּ֔ה סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּכְאַמָּתַ֖יִם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And a wind went forth from YHWH and drove quail from the sea, and let them fall upon the camp, about a day's journey on this side and about a day's journey on that side, around the camp, and about two cubits above the face of the ground.

notes.official: *wərûaḥ nāsaʿ mēʾēṯ YHWH* 'And a wind went forth from YHWH': the same noun as the *rûaḥ* that rested on the elders (vv 17-29), here in its physical sense, so the line has 'wind' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS; overlay `ruach-spirit-on-the-elders-numbers-11`). The repetition joins the two halves of the chapter: YHWH's *rûaḥ* both supplies the leaders and brings the meat. *wayyāḡoz śalwîm min-hayyām* 'and drove quail from the sea': *gûz* 'sweep across' occurs elsewhere only in Ps 90:10. *ûḵəʾammāṯayim ʿal-pənê hāʾāreṣ* 'and about two cubits above the face of the ground' (ASV 'above the face of the earth'). 'ground' follows the clause of central `eretz` for the level from which a height is measured. Whether the quail lay two cubits deep or flew two cubits above the ground (Rashi; Sifre) is left open, as the Hebrew leaves it.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣קָם הָעָ֡ם כָּל־הַיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא וְכָל־הַלַּ֜יְלָה וְכֹ֣ל ׀ י֣וֹם הַֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַיַּֽאַסְפוּ֙ אֶת־הַשְּׂלָ֔ו הַמַּמְעִ֕יט אָסַ֖ף עֲשָׂרָ֣ה חֳמָרִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁטְח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ שָׁט֔וֹחַ סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And the people rose up all that day and all the night and all the next day, and gathered the quail; he who gathered least gathered ten homers; and they spread them out for themselves all around the camp.

notes.official: *hammamʿîṭ ʾāsap̄ ʿăśārâ ḥŏmārîm* 'he who gathered least gathered ten homers': the homer is the largest dry measure, a donkey load. The figure is deliberately excessive. *wayyišṭəḥû lāhem šāṭôaḥ* 'and they spread them out for themselves', to dry the meat.

paragraphs.text: הַבָּשָׂ֗ר עוֹדֶ֙נּוּ֙ בֵּ֣ין שִׁנֵּיהֶ֔ם טֶ֖רֶם יִכָּרֵ֑ת וְאַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ חָרָ֣ה בָעָ֔ם וַיַּ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ בָּעָ֔ם מַכָּ֖ה רַבָּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: While the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of YHWH was kindled against the people, and YHWH struck the people with a very great plague.

notes.official: *habbāśār ʿôḏennû bên šinnêhem ṭerem yikkārēṯ* 'While the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed': *yikkārēṯ* is literally 'was cut off'. The ASV's 'chewed' (NJPS 'chewed') takes it as 'bitten through'; some read 'before the supply was exhausted' (cf. v 20, a whole month). The ASV is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-numbers-11`). *makkâ rabbâ məʾōḏ* 'a very great plague'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא קִבְר֣וֹת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֑ה כִּי־שָׁם֙ קָֽבְר֔וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם הַמִּתְאַוִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And the name of that place was called Qivrot-haTa'avah (Graves of Craving), because there they buried the people who craved.

notes.official: *qiḇrôṯ hattaʾăwâ* 'Qivrot-haTa'avah (Graves of Craving)' = Kibroth-hattaavah (ASV). The gloss follows the Torah rule because the verse gives the etymology in a causal clause (*kî-šām qāḇərû ʾeṯ-hāʿām hammiṯʾawwîm* 'because there they buried the people who craved'). 'Craving' repeats the root *ʾwh* of v 4 ('craved a craving') (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`; central `al-ken-qara-shemah-aetiological-naming-formula-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: מִקִּבְר֧וֹת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֛ה נָסְע֥וּ הָעָ֖ם חֲצֵר֑וֹת וַיִּהְי֖וּ בַּחֲצֵרֽוֹת׃ (פ)

i18n.en: From Qivrot-haTa'avah the people journeyed to Chatzerot; and they stayed at Chatzerot.

notes.official: 'Chatzerot' = Hazeroth (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`; numbers-woh 33:17-18). The station list of Num 33:16-17 records the same two stages.
